text:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: Paging: elevated 5xx and increased latency observed in brazil-south1 egress to ISP-provider-B. Alert rule: egress-errors > 2% over 5m. Investigating now.

Sofia P.: I’m on it. seeing spike at the edge LB before our NAT gateway. top talkers look like multiple small customers, and a sudden jump to one transit peer.

Miguel R.: Confirmed. AS-path shows flapping to ISP-provider-B, traceroutes from our edge -> 100.64.8.1 timeout. Could be peering degradation.

Alex Chen: Is traffic failing to the model instances or just to downstream customers? Initial impact: TTL 5xx on requests routed through that egress region. Embeddings + chat both affected when routed via brazil-south1.

Luca (SRE): Impact assessment: ~18% of requests from brazil-south1 experiencing >500ms and ~3.8% 5xx during the window. Some automatic fallback to other regions is happening but increased latencies observed globally for customers pinned to brazil-south1.

Sofia P.: Quick mitigation options: 1) fail open to region fallback (route to brazil-south1-standby or southamerica-east1), 2) BGP community to prefer alternative transit, 3) short-circuit caching for frequent prefixes. Any constraints?

Miguel R.: We can announce a local BGP withdraw to ISP-provider-B and prefer ISP-provider-A for the affected POP. Need network approval but it’s low-risk.

Alex Chen: For immediate relief, can we flip routing policy on the edge to prefer southamerica-east1 for new sessions? That won’t move pinned sessions but will reduce new placements.

Sofia P.: Agree. I'll request route preference change. @Support Bot please draft a status page message saying "Degraded service in brazil-south1, partial error rates; working on egress peer reroute." Keep it measurable.

Support Bot: Drafting status update (suggested):

```
Status: Degradation in brazil-south1 (egress)
Start: 2026-03-14T15:20:00Z
Summary: We are investigating elevated error rates and latency for requests served from brazil-south1. Our engineers are performing an egress peer reroute to mitigate impact. Some customers may see increased latency or 5xx errors.

What we're doing: Network team is performing a controlled transit preference change and routing failover. We will update as mitigation completes.

Next update: in 15 minutes or when more info available.
```

Luca (SRE): +1 to that. Add "Workaround: Customers can switch to dedicated endpoint in southamerica-east1 or allow multi-region fallback" as a suggestion for high-priority customers.

Customer Ops: Can you also include guidance for customers on pinned model versions? Some are pinned to brazil-south1 and won't automatically fail over. Template for customer notification please.

Sofia P.: Draft customer-facing note:

```
Hi — we’re experiencing higher than normal error rates and latency for requests routed through our brazil-south1 region due to a third-party transit peer disruption. If your application is pinned to brazil-south1, you may see 5xx errors or slower responses. We’re rerouting traffic to an alternate transit provider and updating routing to reduce impact. If you need an immediate workaround, please: 1) Enable multi-region routing in the Console or 2) Temporarily switch to the southamerica-east1 endpoint. Our team will keep you updated and will follow up with a detailed post-incident message.
```

Miguel R.: Network change started: issuing BGP prefer to ISP-provider-A for POP br-south-1-edge now. Monitoring BGP session and egress RTT.

Oncall Bot: Change detected: BGP community set -> prefer-isp-a on br-south-1-edge at 2026-03-14T15:32:10Z.

Sofia P.: Rolling routing preference; new sessions should start preferring alternate transit within ~30s, need ~10min to see full effect. Monitoring 5xx rate.

Luca (SRE): Observability note: runbook step executed: disable long-lived connection reuse for affected proxies to force new routing decisions: `kubectl patch deploy edge-proxy -n pop-br-south --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"force-reconnect":"true"}}}}}'`

Alex Chen: Applied reconnection patch. Forcing reconnects should help clients re-resolve to new path.

Support Bot: Status update posted to status.redwood.ai: "Degraded — Investigating" with the draft copy.

Customer Ops: Sent targeted emails to customers with >500 requests/min pinned to brazil-south1. Template included the workaround steps.

Sofia P.: Observing 5xx rate drop: from 3.8% -> 1.2% in the last 5 minutes. Latency also trending down but still elevated vs baseline.

Miguel R.: BGP sessions stable to ISP-provider-A. No packet loss observed past 15:40Z.

Luca (SRE): Recommendation: keep routing preference in place for 1 hour and continue monitoring. If stable after 1 hour, revert to normal prep references and follow up with incident report.

Alex Chen: Handing off to next on-call for runway: @Luca (SRE) will own monitoring and customer comms for the next 45 minutes. I’ll add details to the incident doc.

Luca (SRE): I’m on handoff. Current status for handoff: mitigation successful, partial residual errors at 0.7%, routing pref applied, status page updated, customers notified. Next update in 30 minutes or if regression.

Oncall Bot: Handoff recorded: previous oncall Sofia P. -> Luca (SRE) at 2026-03-14T16:05:00Z.

Support Bot: Final note to include in post-incident template: cause: third-party transit peer instability affecting egress path for brazil-south1; impact: partial 5xx and higher latency for traffic routed through that peer; mitigations: BGP transit pref change, forced proxy reconnects, customer guidance for multi-region failover.

Sofia P.: Thanks team. I'll draft the postmortem and include recommended action items: automate quicker fallback for pinned sessions, add probing to detect peer jitter, and improve customer-facing runbook for pinned endpoints. :thumbsup:

Customer Ops: Marking customers contacted and opening a follow-up ticket for each impacted account.

Oncall Bot: Thread closed to paging but will remain for updates.
